correctness.rationale: For the exact squared-norm embedding on K_{m+1}, the compressed self-adjoint distortion has norm at most epsilon. The Kantorovich angle inequality for every complex vector is sharp with constant 2sqrt(kappa)/(kappa+1). Consequently every nonzero y has Re(y*Gy)>0 and y*Fy>0, proving nonsingularity of G and positive real part of every eigenvalue of G^-1 F. The explicit two-dimensional SPD example has G=2kappa-epsilon sqrt(kappa)(kappa+1) and F=kappa(kappa+1-2epsilon sqrt(kappa))>0, giving a singular pencil at equality and a negative value immediately above. The kappa=1 boundary is treated separately. The reproducible NumPy script passed 783 supplementary checks; the proof, not the tests, establishes all quantifiers.

value.rationale: The motivating restarted sketched harmonic method explicitly needs right-half-plane harmonic Ritz values. Replacing its SPD epsilon<1/kappa sufficient bound by the exact epsilon<2sqrt(kappa)/(kappa+1) criterion changes the allowed distortion scale from O(kappa^-1) to Theta(kappa^-1/2). Sharp failure directly at the critical threshold shows this numerical safeguard is optimally calibrated, not merely a weak sufficient bound. This is a natural all-dimension matrix pencil robustness classification with a concrete two-state witness. It does not assert overall restarted convergence or an independent sketch-size theorem.
